s1.p2: In the following example, the object **obj** has two properties: **name** and **showMessage**
s1.p4: The only difference with methods is that to call a method, you need to use round brackets after its name, and if the method has formal parameters, you must list the arguments within the round brackets (input data)
s1.p5: ^^As a result of this call, the console will display  “I’m going to the shop”^^
s1.p6: Thus, calling a method differs from calling a regular function only in that the method name must be preceded by the name of the “owner”, separated from the method name by a full stop
s1.p7: All functions (and all variables) in _JS_ have an ‘owner’
s1.p8: Therefore, all functions in _JS_ are methods
s1.p10: For ordinary functions (and variables), the owner is the global object (⟦f3⟧)
s1.p11: Anything that is not ‘privately owned’ belongs to it
s1.p12: If the ‘owner’ is not specified when accessing a property or calling a method, then that owner is the global object
